### 3.1 dispatch_v2 桥接路径（生产主路径）

`dispatch_v2.py:530-570` 的 try 包住 `budget.register_agent` 与

The following claims would **not be supported** by direct evidence and should not be stated as established fact:

| Speculative claim | Why it is unproven |
|---|---|
| "LOOP concurrency caused Desktop to crash" | No Desktop crash is evidenced anywhere; all `exec_failed` events trace to specific, documented causes (access denied, lock contention, auth token, 502 proxy) |
| "High agent count caused the OS/machine to crash or power cycle" | No power/OS crash event exists in any log; the `native_roster.json` shows 154 stale rows from 47+ hours ago — normal historical debris, not crash evidence |
| "The 502 upstream errors were caused by concurrency overload" | The 502s from `127.0.0.1:10100` are from the local `opencodex` proxy; they are consistent with the proxy not yet being ready (cold start / restart), not with load-induced failure |
| "The lifecycle lock contention ([Errno 13]) was caused by too many concurrent agents" | The lock contention burst (~8 events in ~2 seconds, ts 1786565420–1786565680) occurred when a wave attempted simultaneous spawns against a single lock file. This is a **sequencing/locking defect** (no backoff/retry on lock acquisition), not evidence that the count itself caused a crash |
| "The `CreateProcessW (5)` failures were caused by LOOP spawning too many processes" | The error is a permission check, not a resource exhaustion. Windows denies `CreateProcessW` when the calling process lacks elevation or is in a restricted context — unrelated to concurrency count |
| "The supervisor_lost cold_start events indicate the Desktop app crashed" | `supervisor_lost + cold_start:true` means the lifecycle supervisor process exited before writing its first rollout line. This is the expected follow-on from an immediately prior `CreateProcessW (5)` denial in the same wave — not a Desktop app crash |
